proof_boundary: Formal contracts plus reviewed implementation/test correspondence; not compiler refinement or native dependency proof.

online-asr-identity.obligation: Credential edits require a confirmed engine and Alibaba current-epoch endpoint; GLM shares its slot and local engines have no credential slot. Read retry preserves committed engine changes, independent key failure preserves endpoint success, obsolete endpoint completions cannot publish, and debounced writes retain captured identity across a flush-before-switch boundary.
online-asr-identity.assumptions: Three engine kinds with representative Alibaba-domestic/GLM-international combinations, three read batches within two configuration contexts, at most one engine mutation and one read-only retry, two edit/clear attempts and two write invocations. Only a committed engine switch changes context. Retry reissues ERROR fields; READY and PENDING siblings retain their context and may publish after retry. Native success/failure and response order are environmental inputs. Aggregate switch reads settle on first failure or both successes; pending sibling callbacks remain enabled. Engine, endpoint and key failures expose recoverable errors; a key failure preserves identity and an accepted edit retires old key results and clears its key error. Expected identity and write ledgers are independent of implementation readiness. Timer dispatch is abstract in TLC; real hook replay checks 599/600 ms, URL/readiness publication, first-failure busy release, selective retry and deferred flush completion. Switch with both an in-flight save and a second pending draft is excluded and left to debouncer unit regressions. Reachability witnesses are intentional negations, not safety proofs. Region mutation, catalogs, unmount lifecycle, backend storage internals and other windows are outside this bounded companion; no whole-source refinement claim.

engine-status-ownership.obligation: A newer status query or accepted funasr-status event retires older status snapshots. Obsolete status results and errors cannot publish stage, device, GPU or error, start the engine, schedule auto-download or stop current polling. A separate start owner survives native loading progress and running/not-ready polling; a new actual start or accepted terminal state retires it. Three current start rejections reach terminal error and retire pending status queries, preserving that error against late loading. Already issued starts remain issued. Current queries and post-crash recovery still publish.
engine-status-ownership.assumptions: Finite safety companion with independent snapshot and native-start ownership. General bound: three queries, one external ready/loading/error/crashed event and one native loading progress event per issued start. Progress bound: six ordered stopped/loading queries, three native loading events and three rejected starts. Each start spans a loading poll; the last poll completes after terminal start error. Specification snapshot/start epochs are independent of implementation tokens. Obsolete status/start completions remain enabled. The polling flag represents the real 6000 ms interval; loading retains prior polling, ready/error stop it, crash immediately queries and starts polling. Missing status folds the first zero-delay auto-download dispatch into its transition and leaves native download work pending. Issued start ledgers cannot be undone. Four faults remove query retirement, event retirement or awaited-start catch ownership, or incorrectly retire starts on loading progress. Two separately labeled reachability witnesses require current error followed by ready recovery (post-crash recovery is checked by implementation replay) and all three legitimate start failures despite progress/polls plus a dropped late loading snapshot; neither witness is a safety negative. Genuine TLC State schedules replay renderHook, deferred API calls and captured listener, checking public metadata/stage/error, timer and side-effect counts. The ten-loading restart threshold is covered by implementation tests; download generations, cancellation, unmount, other model-state branches, native scheduling, unbounded requests, refinement and liveness are outside this model.

history-stats.obligation: Only the latest started statistics request may publish or log a failure. A current failure retains the last accepted statistics, including when an older success arrives later; a later current success recovers. Unmount retires pending completions.
history-stats.assumptions: Three ordered request identities with success/error as environment inputs; starts abstract mount, history-updated, delete and reprocess refreshes. Actual publication/error ledgers are compared with independent latest-started intent. One unmount invalidates pending work. The reachability witness requires current error logging, accepted recovery and disposal with pending work; it is not a safety negative. TLC counterexample schedules replay the actual page via the API and captured event listener, asserting distinct DOM metrics and console errors. Bounded correspondence only; no unbounded-request, React/native scheduling, refinement or liveness proof. React drops state after unmount, so cleanup replay observes a rejected pending promise instead.

recording.obligation: Reserve, cancel, stop and publish only the current recording session; final UI events cannot regress; disposed recording listeners cannot act.
recording.assumptions: CPAL/OS capture and scheduler termination are environmental inputs; two sessions in TLC, Nat ownership contracts in Lean.

capture.obligation: Native handoff is accepted once; CPAL fallback owns its samples; cap samples and snapshot the selected device.
capture.assumptions: Audio driver success and sample values are inputs; bounded samples represent arbitrary content; RecordingOwnsMonitor begins after the synchronous stop, not the earlier slot reservation.

monitor.obligation: Stop invalidates pending starts; recording ownership prevents late idle-monitor publication; disposed effects never restart monitoring. Monitor restart rechecks active/enabled/mounted/recording/current generation after awaits; late native start is compensated; only the newest overlapping test may resume.
monitor.assumptions: Driver initialization can take time and must observe cancellation; the property guards publication, not an instantaneous hardware shutdown guarantee. Two independent microphone test requests with out-of-order success/failure, one intent retirement and serialized stop/start/compensation phases. Native stop eventually settles; physical instantaneous shutdown is not asserted. A second companion separates two hook instances, a shared native-operation queue, late first start compensation and retired test completion; global native ownership prevents retired cleanup from stopping its replacement.

engine.obligation: Engine/directory changes respect busy capture/download; late starts cannot publish; cloud readiness uses its captured key slot. Present invalid completion metadata is authoritative corrupt state even with a large weight; absent metadata retains legacy compatibility; corrupt/missing status offers explicit repair, and a verified repair becomes ready. Concurrent engine.json field updates preserve committed independent fields and release the transaction after failure.
engine.assumptions: Four engine classes; model output correctness and filesystem/driver/network primitives are outside proof. Ready/error values are environmental inputs. Cache integrity companion partitions absent/valid/invalid manifest and absent/large weights. A positive trace witness reaches repair completion; this reachability target is deliberately false and is not a safety proof. Actual replay calls cache resolvers and explicit download_model verification/atomic manifest publication on temporary local bytes; no GPU/model inference internals are claimed. Configuration writes are within one application process; four independent fields and atomic replacement success/failure are modeled. External writers and arbitrary filesystem durability are outside the mutex contract.

download.obligation: A cancelled download retains ownership/configuration until worker termination; cleanup cannot release a newer task; cancellation/unmount revoke frontend timers and old asynchronous callbacks.
download.assumptions: Filesystem writes and HTTP completion are environmental outcomes; scheduler fairness is required for worker settlement.

directory.obligation: Copy before committing destination; never delete source until current destination and runtime readiness are rechecked.
directory.assumptions: Canonical path resolution and successful copies are trusted filesystem operations; source deletion failures must remain visible.

discovery.obligation: Only the newest request for current provider/engine/auth context may publish; failure retains same-context data. Selective invalidation retires and clears only the selected catalog; polish publication preserves independent assistant ownership and shared catalogs follow polish.
discovery.assumptions: Upstream catalog contents and availability are inputs; finite two-request/context interleavings; HTTP schemas are checked by implementation tests. CatalogDiscoveryOwnership adds two roles, at most two issued requests per role and one selective invalidation per role, success/failure inputs and independent/shared modes. Shared mode projects polish publication/invalidation; independent assistant invalidation is checked in independent mode. Auth/context/unmount remain AsyncSettings obligations. TLC counterexample schedules replay actual hook APIs; this is bounded correspondence, not source refinement. Queued callback cancellation remains implementation-test coverage only; this companion has no scheduler/automatic-dispatch state and makes no queued-cancellation proof claim.

oauth.obligation: Browser/device/refresh owners must remain current; logout and newer login reject old commits and stale fatal refresh.
oauth.assumptions: Identity-provider authentication and cryptography are trusted; generation counters must not wrap; storage durability is a separate obligation.

keys.obligation: Failed keyring write/delete is returned before publishing runtime caches; missing deletes are idempotent; saves, lazy loads and startup restore serialize storage and cache publication. Assistant delayed edits and retry retain captured provider; actual writes serialize; newest provider/read/edit ownership controls read publication. Polish credential reads never write storage; edits capture their provider and retain dirty drafts across switches and failed saves. Retired reads cannot publish.
keys.assumptions: Single keyring operations are atomic; physical OAuth multi-store commits are modeled separately. Getter failure is an unavailable credential, never proof of deletion. Companion model bounds two edits, two provider switches, two independent reads, success/failure and one retry per edit. UI/keyring promises and provider callbacks are checked with actual SettingsPage fixtures; native keyring internals are trusted. Read eligibility snapshots both the dirty draft and request/edit ownership: failed writes retain drafts; only matching successful writes clear them; a read started while dirty cannot become publishable after that clearing. Initial hydration is outside the companion; each provider switch captures a read before subsequent edits or matching save-clear transitions. The same abstract editor ownership machine applies independently to polish and assistant editors; cross-editor last-write ordering is supplied by keyring primitives. Initial profile hydration is tested in the implementation, not added to this companion model.

profile-save.obligation: Each profile update queues its own current version under the same ordering lock; settled disk is latest.
profile-save.assumptions: Debounce timer and atomic filesystem replacement eventually succeed for settlement; Lean proves version ordering over arbitrary Nat updates. Failed writes and generation-owned status/retry are covered by isolated real-filesystem implementation tests; ProfilePersistence models successful writes only. The UI receives revisioned status snapshots after listener registration.

preferences.obligation: Settings controls require a successfully loaded profile; failures retain the blocked state and retry restores saved preferences. Normalize/validate before publication; optional clears are explicit; runtime-only flags do not overwrite other fields.
preferences.assumptions: The valid/invalid abstraction is instantiated by actual validators and unit partitions; it is not a proof of every Rust string/parser branch. The UI workload uses one representative History field, two profile reads, and success/failure inputs; other command workloads start ready and retain the full field partition.

providers.obligation: Custom provider fields validate before mutation; removed provider references resolve to safe existing roles; every LLM/catalog request freezes provider, endpoint and auth choice, and account credentials are resolved from one session.
providers.assumptions: URL parser and provider network behavior are trusted; built-in/custom represent equivalent reference classes, not all server features.

personalization.obligation: Blocked hotwords cannot be relearned automatically; concurrent user corrections survive automatic review; exported data excludes credentials.
personalization.assumptions: Canonical text normalization, JSON schema and learned suggestions are input partitions; explicit user imports/removals may replace user rules.

app-rules.obligation: First matching enabled rule wins; inheritance uses baseline; source window context stays captured.
app-rules.assumptions: Matching predicates are inputs; Lean proves first-match selection for arbitrary rule counts, TLC checks two rules and values.

routing.obligation: Off stays off; explicit actions execute; unknown Auto answers fail open; no-search and captured-window decisions are respected.
routing.assumptions: Classifier/model answers are Yes/No/Unknown inputs; linguistic quality is not proved. Screen and polish overrides are independent variables.

assistant.obligation: Current task owns cancellation; old completion cannot clear it; routed external search/screen preparation joins before dispatch; fresh screen payload uses the foreground snapshot sampled after preparation; only assistant workflow emits chat, validated sources can open.
assistant.assumptions: Network response content and browser opening are trusted external outcomes; request timeout/scheduler progress is required. Integrated search represents external third-party preparation; ModelNative tools run inside the LLM request. Joined preparation remains inside the cancellable assistant future. Foreground identity is sampled after preparation; OS changes after that read are not prevented. Integrated fresh screen preparation is modeled; reused pre-polish descriptions retain prior semantics and have Rust regression evidence.

selection.obligation: Replacement requires exact selection version, text and source window; cancellation owns latest task; raw selection is preserved.
selection.assumptions: OS selection and paste operations are external; two context versions represent arbitrary text, not recognition correctness. State changes use a window-targeted event after publication plus a post-subscription bootstrap snapshot; listener failure falls back to single-flight slow snapshots, checked by implementation tests.

clipboard.obligation: Paste restores clipboard only when clipboard still contains the text owned by that paste; assistant output is never auto-pasted. A completed dictation remains a distinct session/text/original-target queue item while a second assistant occupies the recording slot; all eligible terminal paths schedule a drain; unknown/changed targets and paste failures expose original text for recovery.
clipboard.assumptions: OS clipboard reads/writes and key injection may fail; success means the API acknowledged the operation, not that a foreign application consumed it. Companion output model starts with A processing and independently records B starting/recording. It checks success/error/start-cancel/start-error exits and one focus change. Real queue/controller replay injects only the native paste primitive; source wiring tests establish terminal scheduling correspondence. OS focus remains sampled, and foreign-app consumption is not proved. One production finalizer owns each unique recording session; the queue deduplicates only currently pending session IDs and deliberately permits re-enqueue after a drain. There is no global exactly-once ledger.

history.obligation: Persist only with consent; audio writes may overlap ASR/LLM, but audio resolution and history persistence attempts settle before terminal transcription/subtitle publication and paste authorization; transactions are atomic; shared referenced/leased audio survives GC; reprocess retains captured source. After each SQL transaction, each audio lease count equals the number of independent holders; releasing the first of two shared holders must retain the second. History filter effects retire obsolete requests before debounce dispatch; pending or failed resets block old-offset pagination, current errors remain visible, and retry replaces from offset zero.
history.assumptions: SQLite transactions and successful filesystem deletion are trusted primitives; detailed base bound of five rows, three audio classes and one reprocessor/count-one lease; DB errors retain audio conservatively. Finalization may publish after a failed audio/history write, but must first await its completion. Publication here means terminal transcription/subtitle results and paste authorization; assistant stream chunks and stream done arrive during LLM work and are excluded. Scheduling permits audio I/O to remain pending during LLM work; the model does not prove a wall-clock speedup. HistoryRecords retains its detailed five-row, three audio-class, single-reprocessor/count-one bound. HistoryLeaseInterleavings adds two independent tasks and two shared audio identities; release is DELETE count=1, UPDATE count>1, then commit. Equality is asserted outside the transaction; row deletion and GC interleave only at commit boundaries. Statistics reuse is checked by implementation tests: a retained read connection compares SQLite data_version, aggregate and latency queries share a read transaction, and concurrent changes invalidate cache publication. Database path remains fixed during the process; replacing the open database file is outside this contract. HistoryFilterOwnership adds seed row 1, optional old page row 2, one filter epoch, reset/retry replacement rows 3 and 4, and one normal pagination append row 5. Request identities are old=1/reset=2/retry=3/page=4; repeated retries fold to identity 3. Pagination availability directly follows hasMore, loading and error, independent of the specification pending-reset intent; normal pagination must use the current page epoch and offset two, while reset/retry use offset zero. Native success/failure are inputs. Effect retirement and debounce dispatch are distinct actions; actual replay checks 179/180 ms and public DOM/API behavior. Bounded correspondence only; no source refinement.

windows.obligation: Only current show/hide generations publish; interactive state requires a window; exit signals capture and reaps child.
windows.assumptions: Tauri/Windows window placement and pixel geometry are native outcomes; selection drag/resize is reviewed native delegation, not a pixel-layout proof.

subtitles.obligation: Payloads belong to the current session; late interim cannot undo final; stable/tentative text and offsets must validate.
subtitles.assumptions: Text itself is abstract; driver/ASR model accuracy is external; rendering animations are covered by UI tests, not formal timing proofs.

hotkeys.obligation: Registration roles stay unique; backend follows classification; duplicate presses and stale stop owners cannot stop newer recording.
hotkeys.assumptions: OS key delivery/debounce clock are inputs; all three event kinds get separate configurations; bounded representative registration permutations are explicit.

transport.obligation: Request IDs are required; cancelled replies are ignored; streams validate identity, offsets, prefix, terminal output and sample bounds. One total command deadline covers stdin write, flush and reply read; timeout or cancellation invalidates the owned process and releases the command lock. OpenRouter maps unified reasoning before model heuristics; optional completion limits are omitted; native Anthropic retains its mandatory budget and bounded compatibility fallback.
transport.assumptions: Current bundled servers echo request_id; older incompatible engines need updating. Clock/scheduler/network timeout fairness required; providers may fail. Write/flush/read phases use a three-tick total deadline; successful I/O progress never resets it. Real child-pipe replay checks blocked write, write progress before deadline and cancellation, then installs a fresh server. Scheduler/clock fairness and OS pipe semantics remain environmental assumptions. LlmRequestParameters abstracts validated provider/host classification and recognized parameter errors; live provider defaults/limits are external, with request-capture regressions establishing correspondence.

updater.obligation: Update versions compare by the actual numeric parser; release opening accepts HTTPS GitHub hosts only and reports errors.
updater.assumptions: GitHub release metadata and parsed version components are input partitions; numeric comparison is not a SemVer compliance claim.

ui-preferences.obligation: Theme follows system only in system mode; autostart reports success only after an authoritative confirmation. Mounted theme consumers agree; system changes preserve manual choices and delivered storage preferences synchronize windows.
ui-preferences.assumptions: localStorage/media query/Tauri autostart are platform primitives; visuals/accessibility need UI tests. Failed initial autostart read does not establish a known value. The optional tray startup preference is bound to the abstract preference/profile contracts; login-argument and legacy-default behavior have implementation tests, not a proof of native Windows startup. ThemeSynchronization bounds two windows with two mounted consumers, coalesces delivery to the latest stored preference and applies the DOM atomically. Animation, storage exceptions and unmount cleanup use real hook regressions; there is no delivery liveness or source refinement claim.

gpu-idle.obligation: Enabling at startup or runtime starts an idle window; no unload during commands or native streams; readiness survives suspension; successful next commands reload; stale initial settings reads cannot overwrite edits.
gpu-idle.assumptions: Monotonic time and weakly fair timer/command completion; finite clocks in TLC and unbounded Nat policy in Lean. Native load/free success is an input, not a driver proof. AppWorkflow GpuIdle represents Qwen 0.6B and R2T2 recording as an active stream. Input focus/click ordering is checked by real user-event regression tests; linguistic accuracy is outside proof.
